proposals.name: Network SIS epidemic threshold: R0 = beta*lambda_max/gamma (eigenvalue viewpoint)

statements_history.reason: pgcross proposal intake: SisThresholdCard.compute() -- R0=b*l/g where b=beta (infection rate), l=lambda_max (largest eigenvalue of the network's adjacency matrix), g=gamma (recovery rate); an epidemic is self-sustaining iff R0>1.

parents.evidence: weld/M.01.v1 registers that retained distinction forces the graph-Laplacian L_R = D_W - W on a network. The network-SIS epidemic threshold is an INSTANCE of the same underlying graph-structure math family: it is governed by lambda_max, the largest eigenvalue of the graph's ADJACENCY matrix -- a distinct but structurally related spectral quantity of the SAME graph (not the Laplacian eigenvalue itself; the two are related but not identical spectral objects of one graph). This parent link records that structural kinship (both are spectral-graph-theory results on the same underlying network object), not that weld/M.01.v1 formally derives this threshold or that Wang et al. 2003 is prior to or dependent on Toledo/Genesis in any way.

origin.source: Wang, Y.; Chakrabarti, D.; Wang, C.; Faloutsos, C. (2003). "Epidemic spreading in real networks: An eigenvalue viewpoint". 22nd International Symposium on Reliable Distributed Systems (SRDS'03), pp. 25-34.
origin.label: eigenvalue epidemic threshold theorem

proposals.name: Well-mixed (mean-field) SIR basic reproduction number: R0 = beta/gamma

statements_history.reason: pgcross proposal intake: SirWellMixedCard.compute() -- R0=b/g, the classical mean-field (homogeneous-mixing) SIR reproduction number, disambiguated from the network-SIS threshold (PROP-PGCROSS-EPI-01) by NOT depending on any network spectral quantity.

parents.evidence: EQ-015/M.02.v1 registers the general root state-transition pattern S_{n+1}=F(S_n,u_n,c_n,T_n). The well-mixed SIR compartmental model (susceptible/infected/recovered counts evolving under fixed rates beta, gamma) is a concrete INSTANCE of exactly this pattern: the state is the (S,I,R) compartment vector, F is the SIR flow, and R0=beta/gamma is the threshold condition on whether that transition's infected compartment grows or decays. This is a structural-pattern match (a specific dynamical system instantiating a registered general state-transition form), not a claim that Toledo/Genesis derives or predates Kermack & McKendrick's 1927 result.

origin.source: Kermack, W. O.; McKendrick, A. G. (1927). "A Contribution to the Mathematical Theory of Epidemics". Proceedings of the Royal Society A. 115 (772): 700-721.

proposals.name: Herd immunity threshold: HIT = 1 - 1/R0

statements_history.reason: pgcross proposal intake: HerdImmunityCard.compute() -- hit=1.0-1.0/r; refuses (CLARIFY, never computes) when R0<=1, since a sub-threshold disease has no herd-immunity requirement.

parents.evidence: HIT=1-1/R0 is a direct algebraic consequence of the epidemic-threshold condition R0>1 (the fraction of the population that must be immune so the EFFECTIVE reproduction number R0*(1-HIT) falls to exactly 1) -- a genuine, real mathematical derivation from R0, not merely a reading/instance relation like the two R0 proposals above.

Same algebraic derivation applies regardless of which R0-producing model (network-SIS or well-mixed-SIR) supplied the R0 value -- pgcross's own pipeline/compose.py composes HerdImmunityCard's required R0 slot from EITHER producing card, so both are listed as real parents here, mirroring pgcross's own real composed_from provenance model.

origin.source: Standard result in mathematical epidemiology, commonly reviewed in: Fine, P. E. M. (1993). "Herd immunity: history, theory, practice". Epidemiologic Reviews. 15 (2): 265-302. (The formula itself is a direct algebraic consequence of classical SIR threshold theory and predates this specific review; cited here as a commonly-referenced textbook source, not as the formula's origin.)
origin.label: herd immunity threshold
